source.text: Περὶ δὲ τῆς λογείας τῆς εἰς τοὺς ἁγίους, ὥσπερ διέταξα ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις τῆς Γαλατίας, οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς ποιήσατε.

records.literal_gloss: Concerning now the collection the [one] for the holy ones, just as I directed the churches of the Galatia, so also you do.

en.L: Now concerning the collection for the holy ones: just as I gave orders to the churches of Galatia, so you too must do.
en.B: Now about the collection for God's holy people: you are to follow the instructions I gave the churches in Galatia.
en.R: Now I want to tell you about the money we are collecting for God's people in Jerusalem. Do the same things I told the churches in Galatia to do.

fr.L: Quant à la collecte pour les saints, comme je l’ai ordonné aux églises de la Galatie, ainsi faites, vous aussi.
fr.B: Pour ce qui est de la collecte en faveur du peuple saint de Dieu, suivez, vous aussi, les instructions que j’ai données aux églises de Galatie.
fr.R: Je veux maintenant vous parler de l’argent que nous rassemblons pour le peuple de Dieu à Jérusalem. Faites ce que j’ai demandé aux églises de Galatie.

es.L: Ahora bien, en cuanto a la colecta para los santos: así como ordené a las iglesias de Galacia, así también {{plural_you:hagan|haced}} {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.B: En cuanto a la colecta para el pueblo santo de Dios, {{plural_you:sigan|seguid}} las instrucciones que di a las iglesias de Galacia.
es.R: Ahora quiero {{plural_you:hablarles|hablaros}} del dinero que estamos reuniendo para el pueblo de Dios en Jerusalén. {{plural_you:Hagan|Haced}} lo mismo que les dije a las iglesias de Galacia que hicieran.

decisions.choice: now concerning: Paul takes up another matter, probably one the Corinthians raised in their letter
decisions.reason: The same opening, Περὶ δὲ, marks the matters from their letter in 7:1, 7:25, 8:1 and 12:1, and comes again in verse 12. The article with "collection" suggests that the Corinthians already knew about it and had asked how to go about it.

decisions.choice: collection: money gathered from many contributors for a stated purpose
decisions.reason: λογείας is a rare word, found in documents of the time for collections of money, for example for a temple. It is used only here and in verse 2 in the New Testament. Paul elsewhere calls the same gift a ministry, a sharing and a grace (2 Corinthians 8:4; 9:1, 13; Romans 15:26). It was a free gift, not a tax (2 Corinthians 9:5-7).

decisions.choice: the holy ones: the poor believers in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Verse 3 names Jerusalem as the destination. Paul gathered this gift from his Gentile churches for the poor among the believers there (Romans 15:25-27; 2 Corinthians 8-9; Galatians 2:10). Believers are "holy ones" because God has set them apart as his own (1:2).

decisions.choice: Galatia: the Roman province in the center of what is now Turkey, where Paul had founded churches
decisions.reason: Paul had founded and visited churches in Galatia (Acts 16:6; 18:23; Galatians 1:2). The directions he gave them are not recorded anywhere else; verse 2 is probably what they were.

decisions.choice: holy ones (L); God's holy people (B); God's people (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide rendering of this word, as in 1:2: in current English "saints" suggests unusually good people, not a whole congregation.

decisions.choice: the money we are collecting; in Jerusalem
alternatives: the collection for the holy ones
decisions.reason: Readable says what was being collected and who the holy ones were (m2, m3).

decisions.choice: les saints (L); le peuple saint de Dieu (B); le peuple de Dieu (R); "les églises de Galatie" with a lowercase "église"
decisions.reason: As the term sheet and Colossians: "les saints" today suggests exceptionally holy people, so Balanced and Readable say who they are. The churches are local congregations, so "église" is lowercase.

decisions.choice: la colecta (L, B); el dinero que estamos reuniendo (R)
decisions.reason: The word means money gathered from many givers for a stated purpose (m2); Spanish "colecta" says exactly that, and Readable explains it, as the English does.

decisions.choice: los santos (L); el pueblo santo de Dios (B); el pueblo de Dios (R)
decisions.reason: As in 6:1 and 14:33.

source.text: κατὰ μίαν σαββάτου ἕκαστος ὑμῶν παρ’ ἑαυτῷ τιθέτω θησαυρίζων ὅ τι ἐὰν εὐοδῶται, ἵνα μὴ ὅταν ἔλθω τότε λογεῖαι γίνωνται.

records.literal_gloss: On every one [day] of week each of you by himself let put, storing up whatever he may prosper, so that not when I come then collections take place.

en.L: On the first [day] of every week, let each of you put [something] aside by {{gender:themselves|himself}}, storing up whatever {{gender:they|he}} may prosper [in], so that collections may not take place [only] when I come.
en.B: On the first day of each week, every one of you should put something aside at home, saving as much as you have gained, so that there will be no need to take up collections when I arrive.
en.R: Every Sunday, the first day of the week, each of you should put some money aside at home. Save as much as you can from what you have earned. Then there will be no need to collect money when I come.

fr.L: Le premier [jour] de chaque semaine, que chacun de vous mette [quelque chose] de côté par-devers lui, en mettant en réserve selon qu’il aura prospéré, afin que les collectes ne se fassent pas [seulement] quand je viendrai.
fr.B: Le premier jour de chaque semaine, que chacun de vous mette quelque chose de côté chez lui, en épargnant selon ce qu’il a gagné, afin qu’il n’y ait pas besoin de faire des collectes quand j’arriverai.
fr.R: Chaque dimanche, le premier jour de la semaine, chacun de vous doit mettre de l’argent de côté chez soi. Épargnez autant que vous le pouvez sur ce que vous avez gagné. Ainsi, il n’y aura pas besoin de rassembler de l’argent quand je viendrai.

es.L: Cada primer [día] de la semana, cada uno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} ponga [algo] aparte junto a sí, guardando lo que haya prosperado, para que no se hagan colectas [solo] cuando yo llegue.
es.B: El primer día de cada semana, cada uno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} debe apartar algo en su casa y ahorrar según lo que haya ganado, para que no haya que hacer colectas cuando yo llegue.
es.R: Cada domingo, el primer día de la semana, cada uno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} debe apartar algo de dinero en casa. {{plural_you:Ahorren|Ahorrad}} todo lo que {{plural_you:puedan|podáis}} de lo que {{plural_you:hayan|hayáis}} ganado. Así no habrá que reunir dinero cuando yo llegue.

decisions.choice: on every first day of the week
decisions.reason: σαββάτου is the word for the Sabbath, but it was also used for the week, which ended on the Sabbath. Jewish usage numbered the days, so "day one of the week" is the first day, the day after the Sabbath (Mark 16:2; Luke 24:1). κατὰ with it means "every" such day.

decisions.choice: the first day of the week: the day of Jesus' resurrection, when believers came together
decisions.reason: Jesus rose on the first day of the week (Mark 16:2), and believers met on it (Acts 20:7; compare Revelation 1:10). Paul does not say why he chose that day, but setting money aside on the day they met made it a regular part of their life before God. The day later came to be called Sunday.

decisions.choice: put aside at home, building up a store
alternatives: bring it each week to a common fund at the meeting
decisions.reason: παρ ἑαυτῷ means "by himself", at one's own home, and θησαυρίζων means storing up, saving. Each person was to keep a growing amount ready; the text does not speak of a church treasury.

decisions.choice: as much as one has prospered: in proportion to one's earnings
decisions.reason: εὐοδῶται means to have things go well, to succeed. The gift is measured by what each has gained, as in 2 Corinthians 8:11-12, not set at a fixed amount.

decisions.choice: so that the gathering would be done before Paul came
decisions.reason: Paul did not want his visit taken up with raising money, or the gift to be collected under pressure at the last moment (2 Corinthians 9:5).

decisions.choice: {{gender:themselves|himself}}; {{gender:they|he}}
decisions.reason: The Greek uses masculine forms for "each of you", but the instruction is for every member of the church, women and men. Balanced and Readable say "you", which needs no setting.

decisions.choice: Every Sunday, the first day of the week
alternatives: On the first day of every week
decisions.reason: Readable names the day a young reader knows and keeps the biblical name beside it (m2).

decisions.choice: at home
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "by himself" means here (m3). Literal keeps the Greek expression.

decisions.choice: "chacun de vous … par-devers lui … qu’il", with no gender setting
decisions.reason: The English needs {{gender:themselves|himself}} and {{gender:they|he}} at Literal. In French "chacun" already means every member of the church, women and men, and the "lui" and "il" that refer back to it are ordinary generic French, so no span is used (style guide 7).

decisions.choice: junto a sí, haya prosperado, no gender span
decisions.reason: The English gender spans ({{gender:themselves|himself}}, {{gender:they|he}}) have nothing to change in Spanish: "cada uno", "junto a sí" and the verb are the ordinary forms for anyone, man or woman, as in 14:4.

source.text: ὅταν δὲ παραγένωμαι, οὓς ἐὰν δοκιμάσητε δι’ ἐπιστολῶν, τούτους πέμψω ἀπενεγκεῖν τὴν χάριν ὑμῶν εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ·

records.literal_gloss: When and I arrive, whomever you approve through letters, these I will send to carry the grace of you to Jerusalem;

en.L: And when I arrive, whomever you approve through letters, these I will send to carry your grace to Jerusalem.
en.B: When I arrive, I will send the people you have approved, with your letters to recommend them, to take your gift of grace to Jerusalem.
en.R: When I get there, you should choose people you trust, and write letters to say that you trust them. I will send them to Jerusalem with your generous gift.

fr.L: Et quand je serai arrivé, ceux que vous aurez approuvés par des lettres, ceux-là je les enverrai porter votre grâce à Jérusalem.
fr.B: Quand je serai arrivé, j’enverrai les personnes que vous aurez approuvées, avec vos lettres pour les recommander, porter à Jérusalem votre don, fruit de la grâce.
fr.R: Quand je serai là, choisissez des personnes en qui vous avez confiance, et écrivez des lettres pour dire que vous leur faites confiance. Je les enverrai à Jérusalem avec votre don généreux.

es.L: Y cuando llegue, a los que {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:aprueben|aprobéis}} por medio de cartas, a estos enviaré para llevar {{plural_you:la gracia de ustedes|vuestra gracia}} a Jerusalén.
es.B: Cuando llegue, enviaré a las personas que {{plural_you:ustedes hayan|vosotros hayáis}} aprobado, con cartas {{plural_you:suyas|vuestras}} que las recomienden, para que lleven a Jerusalén {{plural_you:su donativo de gracia|vuestro donativo de gracia}}.
es.R: Cuando yo llegue, {{plural_you:ustedes deben|vosotros debéis}} escoger a personas de confianza y escribir cartas para decir que {{plural_you:confían|confiáis}} en ellas. Yo las enviaré a Jerusalén con {{plural_you:su generoso donativo|vuestro generoso donativo}}.

decisions.choice: your gift: the generous gift that grace produces
decisions.reason: χάριν is the word for grace. Here it is the money the Corinthians give, which Paul calls a grace because it is a free and generous gift and because God's grace is at work in it (2 Corinthians 8:1, 6-7, 19).

decisions.choice: letters from the Corinthians, recommending the people they approve
alternatives: letters from Paul, sent with the people they approve
decisions.reason: The phrase δι ἐπιστολῶν ("through letters") can go with "you approve" or with "I will send". The SBLGNT puts a comma after it, which joins it to the first: the church approves its delegates and gives them letters to vouch for them in Jerusalem. Read with the second, Paul himself would write letters to send with them. Paul was ready to send them on their own (verse 4), which suits letters from the church, but both readings make good sense.

decisions.choice: letters of recommendation for trusted messengers
decisions.reason: Churches sent such letters with travelers they trusted (Acts 18:27; 2 Corinthians 3:1). The church, not Paul, chose who would carry its money, so that no one could accuse Paul of mishandling it (2 Corinthians 8:19-21).

decisions.choice: approve: accept after testing
decisions.reason: δοκιμάσητε is to test and so approve; it belongs to the word family of "approved" in 11:19 and 2 Corinthians 10:18.

decisions.choice: grace (L); gift of grace (B); generous gift (R)
decisions.reason: As in 2 Corinthians 8:6, 19: Literal keeps the key term; Balanced says "gift of grace", which keeps the word and makes clear that a gift is meant (m1); Readable says "generous gift".

decisions.choice: with your letters to recommend them (B); write letters to say that you trust them (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the letters were for, following the SBLGNT punctuation (m2).

decisions.choice: votre don, fruit de la grâce (B)
decisions.reason: The English "gift of grace" keeps the key term and says that a gift is meant (m1). "Votre don de grâce" would read in French as a gift God gives; "fruit de la grâce" keeps "grâce" and says that the Corinthians' gift is what grace produces.

decisions.choice: gracia (L); donativo de gracia (B); generoso donativo (R)
decisions.reason: "Gracia" is a key term; here it means the generous gift that grace produces (m1). Literal keeps "gracia", Balanced "donativo de gracia" and Readable "generoso donativo", as the English says "gift of grace" and "generous gift".

source.text: ἐὰν δὲ ἄξιον ᾖ τοῦ κἀμὲ πορεύεσθαι, σὺν ἐμοὶ πορεύσονται.

records.literal_gloss: If and fitting it is for the me also to go, with me they will go.

en.L: And if it is fitting for me also to go, they will go with me.
en.B: If it seems right for me to go as well, they will travel with me.
en.R: If it seems best for me to go too, they can go with me.

fr.L: Et s’il convient que moi aussi j’y aille, ils iront avec moi.
fr.B: S’il paraît bon que j’y aille moi aussi, ils feront le voyage avec moi.
fr.R: S’il vaut mieux que j’y aille aussi, ils pourront partir avec moi.

es.L: Y si es conveniente que yo también vaya, irán conmigo.
es.B: Si parece oportuno que yo también vaya, viajarán conmigo.
es.R: Si parece mejor que yo vaya también, pueden ir conmigo.

decisions.choice: fitting: if it seems right in the circumstances
alternatives: worthwhile: if the gift is large enough to justify Paul's going
decisions.reason: ἄξιον means worthy or fitting. Paul may mean simply "if it seems best", or he may make his going depend on the size of the gift. He leaves it open.

decisions.choice: Paul did in the end go to Jerusalem with the gift
decisions.reason: When he wrote Romans, Paul was about to take the collection to Jerusalem himself (Romans 15:25-28), and Acts names men from several churches who traveled with him (Acts 20:4; 24:17).

source.text: Ἐλεύσομαι δὲ πρὸς ὑμᾶς ὅταν Μακεδονίαν διέλθω, Μακεδονίαν γὰρ διέρχομαι, πρὸς ὑμᾶς δὲ τυχὸν παραμενῶ ἢ καὶ παραχειμάσω, ἵνα ὑμεῖς με προπέμψητε οὗ ἐὰν πορεύωμαι.

records.literal_gloss: I will come and to you when Macedonia I pass through, Macedonia for I am passing through, \v 6 with you and perhaps I will stay or even spend the winter, so that you me may send on wherever I may go.

en.L: And I will come to you when I pass through Macedonia, for I am passing through Macedonia; \v 6 and with you perhaps I will stay, or even spend the winter, so that you may send me on [my way] wherever I go.
en.B: I will come to you after I have gone through Macedonia, since my route lies through Macedonia. \v 6 I may stay with you for a while, perhaps even for the winter. Then you can send me on, with what I need, to wherever I go next.
en.R: I will visit you after I travel through Macedonia, because that is the way I plan to go. \v 6 I may stay with you for a while, maybe even for the whole winter. Then you can give me what I need for the next part of my trip, wherever I go.

fr.L: Et je viendrai chez vous quand j’aurai traversé la Macédoine, car je traverse la Macédoine ; \v 6 et chez vous peut-être je resterai, ou même je passerai l’hiver, afin que vous m’aidiez à poursuivre [ma route] là où j’irai.
fr.B: Je viendrai chez vous après avoir traversé la Macédoine, puisque ma route passe par la Macédoine. \v 6 Il se peut que je reste quelque temps chez vous, peut-être même pour l’hiver. Vous pourrez alors m’aider à repartir, avec ce dont j’aurai besoin, là où j’irai ensuite.
fr.R: Je viendrai vous voir après avoir voyagé en Macédoine, parce que c’est le chemin que je compte prendre. \v 6 Je resterai peut-être un moment chez vous, peut-être même pendant tout l’hiver. Ensuite, vous pourrez me donner ce qu’il me faut pour la suite de mon voyage, quel que soit l’endroit où j’irai.

es.L: E iré a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} cuando haya pasado por Macedonia, porque paso por Macedonia; \v 6 y con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} quizá me quede, o incluso pase el invierno, para que {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} me {{plural_you:encaminen|encaminéis}} adondequiera que vaya.
es.B: Iré a {{plural_you:verlos|veros}} después de pasar por Macedonia, ya que mi camino pasa por Macedonia. \v 6 Puede que me quede con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} un tiempo, quizá incluso todo el invierno. Luego {{plural_you:podrán|podréis}} ayudarme a seguir el viaje, con lo que necesite, adondequiera que vaya después.
es.R: Iré a {{plural_you:visitarlos|visitaros}} después de viajar por Macedonia, porque ese es el camino que pienso tomar. \v 6 Puede que me quede con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} un tiempo, quizá todo el invierno. Después {{plural_you:podrán|podréis}} darme lo que necesite para la siguiente parte del viaje, adondequiera que vaya.

decisions.choice: Paul's route: north from Ephesus through Macedonia, then south to Corinth
decisions.reason: Macedonia was the Roman province north of Achaia, with the churches of Philippi and Thessalonica. Acts 19:21 and 20:1-3 describe this journey. 2 Corinthians 1:15-16 tells of a later change of plan, which Paul had to explain.

decisions.choice: I am going through: a settled plan, not a journey already under way
alternatives: I am now traveling through Macedonia
decisions.reason: The present διέρχομαι states what Paul has decided to do. Verse 8 shows he is still in Ephesus. Some later manuscripts add a note at the end of the letter saying it was written from Philippi, which probably comes from misreading this verse.

decisions.choice: spend the winter: travel by sea stopped in winter
decisions.reason: Ships seldom sailed in the winter months (Acts 27:9-12; 28:11), so travelers often stayed where they were until spring. Acts 20:2-3 says Paul spent three months in Greece.

decisions.choice: send on: help a traveler on the way with supplies and company
decisions.reason: προπέμψητε was the regular word for a church's help to a traveling preacher: food, money, sometimes companions (Romans 15:24; 2 Corinthians 1:16; Titus 3:13).

decisions.choice: give me what I need for the next part of my trip
decisions.reason: Readable says what "sending on" involved (m4).

decisions.choice: m’aider à poursuivre [ma route] (L); m’aider à repartir, avec ce dont j’aurai besoin (B); the same verb in verse 11
decisions.reason: The verb means helping a traveller on the way with supplies and company (m4). "Accompagner" would say only that they go with him; "aider à poursuivre sa route" covers the help.

decisions.choice: encaminar
decisions.reason: The verb means to help a traveler on the way with supplies and company (m4). Spanish "encaminar" (to set someone on the road) keeps one verb for Literal here and in verse 11; Balanced and Readable spell out the help.

source.text: οὐ θέλω γὰρ ὑμᾶς ἄρτι ἐν παρόδῳ ἰδεῖν, ἐλπίζω γὰρ χρόνον τινὰ ἐπιμεῖναι πρὸς ὑμᾶς, ἐὰν ὁ κύριος ἐπιτρέψῃ.

records.literal_gloss: Not I want for you now in passing to see, I hope for time some to remain with you, if the Lord permits.

en.L: For I do not want to see you now in passing, for I hope to remain some time with you, if the Lord permits.
en.B: This time I do not want to see you only briefly, on my way somewhere else; I hope to stay with you for a while, if the Lord allows.
en.R: I do not want to stop for only a short visit this time. If the Lord lets me, I hope to stay with you for a good while.

fr.L: Car je ne veux pas vous voir maintenant en passant, car j’espère rester quelque temps auprès de vous, si le Seigneur le permet.
fr.B: Cette fois, je ne veux pas vous voir seulement en passant, sur la route vers un autre lieu ; j’espère rester quelque temps auprès de vous, si le Seigneur le permet.
fr.R: Cette fois, je ne veux pas m’arrêter seulement pour une courte visite. Si le Seigneur me le permet, j’espère rester assez longtemps avec vous.

es.L: Porque no quiero {{plural_you:verlos|veros}} ahora de paso, pues espero quedarme algún tiempo con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, si el Señor [lo] permite.
es.B: Esta vez no quiero {{plural_you:verlos|veros}} solo un momento, de camino a otro lugar; espero quedarme un tiempo con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, si el Señor lo permite.
es.R: Esta vez no quiero hacer solo una visita corta. Si el Señor me lo permite, espero quedarme bastante tiempo con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

decisions.choice: now: this time Paul does not want a short visit on the way to somewhere else
alternatives: Paul does not want to come right now, straight from Ephesus, for a short stop
decisions.reason: ἄρτι ("now") may set this visit against a quick one he once had in mind, or simply mean "this time". Either way his wish is to stay longer.

decisions.choice: Paul's plans depend on the Lord's will
decisions.reason: Paul makes his travel depend on what the Lord allows, as in 4:19 and as James 4:15 teaches. "The Lord" here is most likely Christ, as usually in Paul's letters.

decisions.choice: This time (B); this time (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out the sense of "now" (m1).

source.text: ἐπιμενῶ δὲ ἐν Ἐφέσῳ ἕως τῆς πεντηκοστῆς·

records.literal_gloss: I will remain and in Ephesus until the Pentecost;

en.L: But I will remain in Ephesus until Pentecost.
en.B: But I will stay on here in Ephesus until Pentecost.
en.R: But I will stay here in Ephesus until the Jewish festival of Pentecost, in late spring.

fr.L: Mais je resterai à Éphèse jusqu’à la Pentecôte.
fr.B: Mais je resterai ici, à Éphèse, jusqu’à la Pentecôte.
fr.R: Mais je resterai ici, à Éphèse, jusqu’à la Pentecôte, la fête juive de la fin du printemps.

es.L: Pero me quedaré en Éfeso hasta Pentecostés.
es.B: Pero me quedaré aquí en Éfeso hasta Pentecostés.
es.R: Pero me quedaré aquí en Éfeso hasta la fiesta judía de Pentecostés, al final de la primavera.

decisions.choice: Ephesus: Paul writes from there
decisions.reason: Ephesus was the chief city of the province of Asia, where Paul worked for more than two years (Acts 19:8-10). This verse shows that he wrote the letter there.

decisions.choice: Pentecost: the Jewish Feast of Weeks, fifty days after Passover
decisions.reason: πεντηκοστῆς means "fiftieth". The feast came fifty days after Passover (Leviticus 23:15-16; Deuteronomy 16:9-10), in late spring. Paul still marks time by the Jewish festivals (compare 5:7-8), and the reference suggests he wrote in the spring.

decisions.choice: here
decisions.reason: Paul is in Ephesus as he writes (m1).

decisions.choice: the Jewish festival of Pentecost, in late spring
decisions.reason: Readable says what Pentecost was and when it fell (m2).

source.text: θύρα γάρ μοι ἀνέῳγεν μεγάλη καὶ ἐνεργής, καὶ ἀντικείμενοι πολλοί.

records.literal_gloss: A door for to me has opened great and effective, and opposing [ones] many.

en.L: For a door has opened to me, great and effective, and [there are] many who oppose [me].
en.B: A great door stands open here for work that bears fruit, and many are working against me.
en.R: God has given me a big opportunity to do work here that is bearing fruit. And many people are fighting against me.

fr.L: Car une porte s’est ouverte pour moi, grande et efficace, et [il y a] beaucoup d’adversaires.
fr.B: Une grande porte s’est ouverte ici pour un travail qui porte du fruit, et les adversaires sont nombreux.
fr.R: Dieu m’a donné ici une belle occasion de faire un travail qui porte du fruit. Et beaucoup de gens luttent contre moi.

es.L: Porque se me ha abierto una puerta grande y eficaz, y [hay] muchos adversarios.
es.B: Aquí tengo abierta una gran puerta para un trabajo que da fruto, y son muchos los que se oponen.
es.R: Dios me ha dado una gran oportunidad para hacer aquí un trabajo que está dando fruto. Y hay mucha gente luchando contra mí.

decisions.choice: an open door: an opportunity to spread the gospel
decisions.reason: Paul uses the same picture in 2 Corinthians 2:12 and Colossians 4:3, where it is the Lord or God who opens the door. In Ephesus many were hearing the message (Acts 19:10, 20).

decisions.choice: effective: an opening that leads to work that achieves much
decisions.reason: ἐνεργής means active, effective, producing results. The door is not only wide but leads to real work.

decisions.choice: the opposition Paul faced in Ephesus
decisions.reason: Acts 19:9 and 19:23-41 tell of resistance in the synagogue and of a riot in the city, and Paul speaks of having "fought wild beasts" there (15:32; compare 2 Corinthians 1:8).

decisions.choice: and: the opposition is part of why Paul stays, not a reason to leave
alternatives: but: in spite of the opponents
decisions.reason: Paul joins the two with "and": the open door and the many opponents together keep him in Ephesus for now.

decisions.choice: God has given me a big opportunity
alternatives: a door has opened to me
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture (m1) and names God as the one who opens the door, as in Colossians 4:3.

decisions.choice: work that bears fruit (B); work ... that is bearing fruit (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what kind of door it is (m2).

source.text: Ἐὰν δὲ ἔλθῃ Τιμόθεος, βλέπετε ἵνα ἀφόβως γένηται πρὸς ὑμᾶς, τὸ γὰρ ἔργον κυρίου ἐργάζεται ὡς κἀγώ·

records.literal_gloss: If and comes Timothy, see that without fear he may be with you; the for work of [the] Lord he works as also I;

en.L: Now if Timothy comes, see that he is with you without fear; for he is working the work of [the] Lord, as I also [am].
en.B: If Timothy comes, take care that he can be with you without fear, because the work he does is the Lord's work, just as mine is.
en.R: Timothy may come to visit you. If he does, make sure he does not feel afraid while he is with you. He works for the Lord, the same as I do.

fr.L: Et si Timothée vient, veillez à ce qu’il soit sans crainte auprès de vous ; car il travaille à l’œuvre du Seigneur, comme moi aussi.
fr.B: Si Timothée vient, faites en sorte qu’il puisse être parmi vous sans rien craindre, car le travail qu’il fait est l’œuvre du Seigneur, tout comme le mien.
fr.R: Timothée viendra peut-être vous voir. S’il vient, faites en sorte qu’il n’ait pas peur quand il sera avec vous. Il travaille pour le Seigneur, comme moi.

es.L: Y si llega Timoteo, {{plural_you:procuren|procurad}} que esté sin temor con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, porque hace la obra del Señor, así como yo.
es.B: Si llega Timoteo, {{plural_you:procuren|procurad}} que pueda estar con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} sin temor, porque el trabajo que hace es la obra del Señor, igual que el mío.
es.R: Puede que Timoteo vaya a {{plural_you:visitarlos|visitaros}}. Si va, {{plural_you:asegúrense|aseguraos}} de que no sienta miedo mientras esté con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Él trabaja para el Señor, igual que yo.

decisions.choice: if Timothy comes: his arrival was not certain
decisions.reason: Ἐὰν means "if". Paul had sent Timothy (4:17), who went by way of Macedonia (Acts 19:22) and might arrive after the letter, or might be delayed.

decisions.choice: without fear: the Corinthians are not to make Timothy's visit hard for him
decisions.reason: Some in Corinth were arrogant toward Paul (4:18-19), and Timothy was young (1 Timothy 4:12). Coming as Paul's representative, he might meet the same contempt. Paul asks the church to receive him in a way that leaves him nothing to fear.

decisions.choice: the Lord's work: Timothy serves Christ as Paul does
decisions.reason: "The work of the Lord" is the building of the church, as in 15:58 and 3:9-15. ὡς κἀγώ puts Timothy's work on a level with Paul's own.

source.text: μή τις οὖν αὐτὸν ἐξουθενήσῃ.

records.literal_gloss: Not anyone therefore him should despise.

en.L: So let no one despise him.
en.B: No one, then, should look down on him.
en.R: So do not let anyone treat him as unimportant.

fr.L: Que personne donc ne le méprise.
fr.B: Que personne, donc, ne le regarde de haut.
fr.R: Alors, ne laissez personne le traiter comme quelqu’un sans importance.

es.L: Así que nadie lo menosprecie.
es.B: Que nadie, entonces, lo mire con desprecio.
es.R: Así que no {{plural_you:dejen|dejéis}} que nadie lo trate como si no fuera importante.

decisions.choice: despise: treat as of no account
decisions.reason: ἐξουθενήσῃ means to treat someone as worthless (1:28; 6:4). The Corinthians are not to dismiss Timothy because he is young or because he is not Paul.

source.text: προπέμψατε δὲ αὐτὸν ἐν εἰρήνῃ, ἵνα ἔλθῃ πρός με, ἐκδέχομαι γὰρ αὐτὸν μετὰ τῶν ἀδελφῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Send on and him in peace, so that he may come to me, I am expecting for him with the brothers.

en.L: But send him on [his way] in peace, so that he may come to me; for I am expecting him with the brothers.
en.B: See him off in peace, with what he needs for the road, so that he can come back to me; I am looking for him to return with the brothers.
en.R: Help him on his trip and send him off in peace, so that he can come back to me. I am expecting him to come back with the brothers.

fr.L: Mais aidez-le à poursuivre [sa route] en paix, afin qu’il vienne vers moi ; car je l’attends avec les frères.
fr.B: Aidez-le à repartir en paix, avec ce dont il a besoin pour la route, afin qu’il puisse revenir auprès de moi : j’attends qu’il revienne avec les frères.
fr.R: Aidez-le pour son voyage et laissez-le partir en paix, pour qu’il puisse revenir auprès de moi. J’attends qu’il revienne avec les frères.

es.L: Más bien {{plural_you:encamínenlo|encaminadlo}} en paz, para que venga a mí, porque lo espero con los hermanos.
es.B: {{plural_you:Despídanlo|Despedidlo}} en paz, con lo que necesite para el camino, para que pueda volver a mí; espero que regrese con los hermanos.
es.R: {{plural_you:Ayúdenlo|Ayudadlo}} en su viaje y {{plural_you:despídanlo|despedidlo}} en paz, para que pueda volver a mí. Espero que regrese con los hermanos.

decisions.choice: send on: help on the journey, as in verse 6
decisions.reason: The church was to supply what Timothy needed for the return journey.

decisions.choice: in peace: with good will, on good terms
decisions.reason: To send someone off ἐν εἰρήνῃ was to part on good terms and with a blessing (Acts 15:33). Paul wants Timothy to leave with no quarrel between him and the church.

decisions.choice: Timothy will come back with the brothers
alternatives: Paul and the brothers with him are waiting for Timothy
decisions.reason: "With the brothers" can go with "him" or with "I". Verse 12 speaks of brothers going to Corinth, probably Stephanas, Fortunatus and Achaicus, who were with Paul (verse 17) and would carry this letter. Paul most likely expects Timothy to return with them. The Greek can also mean that Paul and the believers with him are waiting.

decisions.choice: the brothers, with no setting
decisions.reason: These are a particular group of men traveling with Timothy, probably the three named in verse 17 (m3), so the inclusive form does not apply, as with the brothers sent in 2 Corinthians 8:18-23.

decisions.choice: come back to me
decisions.reason: Timothy had been sent from Paul and was returning to him (4:17).

source.text: Περὶ δὲ Ἀπολλῶ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ, πολλὰ παρεκάλεσα αὐτὸν ἵνα ἔλθῃ πρὸς ὑμᾶς μετὰ τῶν ἀδελφῶν· καὶ πάντως οὐκ ἦν θέλημα ἵνα νῦν ἔλθῃ, ἐλεύσεται δὲ ὅταν εὐκαιρήσῃ.

records.literal_gloss: Concerning and Apollos the brother, much I urged him that he come to you with the brothers; and at all not was will that now he come, he will come but when he has opportunity.

en.L: Now concerning Apollos the brother, I urged him much to come to you with the brothers; and it was not at all [the] will that he come now, but he will come when he has opportunity.
en.B: As for our brother Apollos, I pressed him again and again to visit you along with the brothers. But he was not at all willing to come at this time; he will come when a good opportunity arises.
en.R: And here is news about our brother Apollos. I begged him many times to go and visit you with the brothers. But he did not want to go now. He will come when the time is right.

fr.L: Quant à Apollos, le frère, je l’ai beaucoup exhorté à venir chez vous avec les frères ; et ce n’était absolument pas [la] volonté qu’il vienne maintenant, mais il viendra quand il en aura l’occasion.
fr.B: Quant à notre frère Apollos, je l’ai pressé à plusieurs reprises de venir chez vous avec les frères. Mais il ne voulait absolument pas venir maintenant ; il viendra quand une bonne occasion se présentera.
fr.R: Et voici des nouvelles de notre frère Apollos. Je lui ai demandé plusieurs fois d’aller vous voir avec les frères. Mais il ne voulait pas y aller maintenant. Il viendra quand le moment sera bon.

es.L: Y en cuanto al hermano Apolos, le rogué mucho que fuera a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} con los hermanos; y de ningún modo era [su] voluntad ir ahora, pero irá cuando tenga oportunidad.
es.B: En cuanto a nuestro hermano Apolos, le insistí una y otra vez en que fuera a {{plural_you:visitarlos|visitaros}} con los hermanos. Pero él no quiso de ninguna manera ir por ahora; irá cuando se le presente una buena oportunidad.
es.R: Y ahora, noticias de nuestro hermano Apolos. Le rogué muchas veces que fuera a {{plural_you:visitarlos|visitaros}} con los hermanos. Pero él no quiso ir ahora. Irá cuando sea el momento oportuno.

decisions.choice: now concerning: another matter, perhaps a request in the Corinthians' letter
decisions.reason: Περὶ δὲ opens a new subject as in verse 1. The Corinthians may have asked for Apollos to come back.

decisions.choice: Apollos: a fellow worker, now with Paul in Ephesus
decisions.reason: Acts 18:24-28 describes Apollos as an eloquent teacher who worked in Corinth after Paul. Some there said "I am for Apollos" (1:12; 3:4), but Paul treats him as a fellow worker (3:5-9), urges him to go, and does not stand in his way.

decisions.choice: Apollos's own will: he did not want to come now
alternatives: God's will: it was not God's will that he come now
decisions.reason: The Greek has only θέλημα ("will"), without saying whose. The next words, "he will come when he has opportunity", speak of Apollos's own choice, so the will is most likely his. But early Christian writers sometimes used the word on its own for God's will (compare Romans 2:18), and some read it that way here. Either way Paul is not to blame for Apollos's staying away.

decisions.choice: when he has a good opportunity
decisions.reason: εὐκαιρήσῃ means to have the right time or the leisure for something (Mark 6:31).

decisions.choice: our brother
decisions.reason: Apollos is a brother to Paul and to the church alike; English needs "our" where the Greek has "the".

decisions.choice: the brothers, with no setting
decisions.reason: The brothers going to Corinth are probably the three men of verse 17, as in verse 11, so the inclusive form does not apply.

decisions.choice: he was not at all willing (B); he did not want (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable follow the reading that the will is Apollos's (m3). Literal keeps the Greek's open wording.

source.text: Γρηγορεῖτε, στήκετε ἐν τῇ πίστει, ἀνδρίζεσθε, κραταιοῦσθε.

records.literal_gloss: Keep awake, stand firm in the faith, act like men, be strong.

en.L: Keep awake, stand firm in the faith, {{gender:be courageous|act like men}}, be strong.
en.B: Stay alert. Hold your ground in the faith. Be brave and be strong.
en.R: Watch out and stay awake. Keep standing firm in your faith. Be brave and strong.

fr.L: Veillez, tenez ferme dans la foi, {{gender:soyez courageux|conduisez-vous en hommes}}, soyez forts.
fr.B: Restez vigilants. Tenez vos positions dans la foi. Soyez courageux et forts.
fr.R: Faites attention et restez éveillés. Continuez à tenir ferme dans votre foi. Soyez courageux et forts.

es.L: {{plural_you:Velen|Velad}}, {{plural_you:estén|estad}} firmes en la fe, {{plural_you:sean|sed}} {{gender:valientes|varoniles}}, {{plural_you:fortalézcanse|fortaleceos}}.
es.B: {{plural_you:Estén|Estad}} alerta. {{plural_you:Manténganse|Manteneos}} firmes en la fe. {{plural_you:Sean|Sed}} valientes y fuertes.
es.R: {{plural_you:Estén|Estad}} atentos y {{plural_you:manténganse|manteneos}} despiertos. {{plural_you:Sigan|Seguid}} firmes en {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} fe. {{plural_you:Sean|Sed}} valientes y fuertes.

decisions.choice: keep awake: be alert to danger and ready for the Lord's coming
decisions.reason: Γρηγορεῖτε is to stay awake, and so to be watchful. Jesus uses it of readiness for his coming (Matthew 24:42), and Paul of alertness in a world that sleeps (1 Thessalonians 5:6).

decisions.choice: the faith: their trust in Christ, grounded in the gospel they received
alternatives: the body of teaching believed only
decisions.reason: With the article, πίστει can mean the trust believers have or what they believe. Paul has just spoken of the gospel "in which you stand" (15:1-2); standing firm in the faith holds both together.

decisions.choice: be courageous
alternatives: behave as men (and not women) should
decisions.reason: ἀνδρίζεσθε is formed from the word for a man and once meant "act like a man". In use it meant to be brave: the Greek Old Testament uses it for courage given to all God's people (Psalm 31:25, Greek 30:25). Paul is writing to the whole church, women and men, and calls them all to courage.

decisions.choice: an echo of the Old Testament call to be brave and strong
decisions.reason: ἀνδρίζεσθε and κραταιοῦσθε together recall the Greek Old Testament's "be strong and courageous", spoken to Joshua and Israel (Deuteronomy 31:6; Joshua 1:6-9) and in Psalm 31:25. The second verb is passive in form: "be made strong", strength that comes from God.

decisions.choice: {{gender:be courageous|act like men}} (L); be brave (B, R)
decisions.reason: The meaning is courage, asked of the whole church (m3). Literal offers the traditional form, which shows how the word is built, as its alternative; Balanced and Readable say "be brave", which needs no setting.

decisions.choice: Hold your ground
decisions.reason: A soldier's picture for refusing to give way, fitting the commands around it.

decisions.choice: {{gender:soyez courageux|conduisez-vous en hommes}} (L)
decisions.reason: As in English: the command is courage, asked of the whole church (m3), and the alternative shows how the word is built. "Courageux" in the masculine plural is the ordinary French form for a mixed group.

decisions.choice: Tenez vos positions (B)
decisions.reason: Keeps the soldier's picture of refusing to give way, as the English "Hold your ground" does; Literal and Readable say "tenir ferme".

decisions.choice: {{gender:valientes|varoniles}}
decisions.reason: The Greek verb is built on the word for "man" but means be courageous (m3), and the English Literal offers both through a gender span. Spanish has the same two wordings, "valientes" and "varoniles", and the span holds only the adjective so that it does not overlap the plural_you span on the verb.

decisions.choice: velar (L); estar alerta (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the settled New Testament terms for this verb: "velar" at Literal, "estar alerta" at Balanced and Readable.

source.text: πάντα ὑμῶν ἐν ἀγάπῃ γινέσθω.

records.literal_gloss: All [things] of you in love let be done.

en.L: Let all your [actions] be done in love.
en.B: Whatever you do, do it in love.
en.R: Let love show in everything you do.

fr.L: Que toutes vos [actions] se fassent dans l’amour.
fr.B: Quoi que vous fassiez, faites-le avec amour.
fr.R: Que l’amour se voie dans tout ce que vous faites.

es.L: Todas {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} [acciones] háganse en amor.
es.B: Todo lo que {{plural_you:hagan|hagáis}}, {{plural_you:háganlo|hacedlo}} con amor.
es.R: Que el amor se vea en todo lo que {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}}.

decisions.choice: in love: love as the way all they do is done
decisions.reason: ἐν ἀγάπῃ describes the manner and setting of all their actions. It sums up chapter 13 and answers the divisions, pride and selfishness the letter has addressed (8:1; 13:4-7).

decisions.choice: Let love show in
decisions.reason: Readable puts love first so that the command is plain to a young reader.

source.text: Παρακαλῶ δὲ ὑμᾶς, ἀδελφοί· οἴδατε τὴν οἰκίαν Στεφανᾶ, ὅτι ἐστὶν ἀπαρχὴ τῆς Ἀχαΐας καὶ εἰς διακονίαν τοῖς ἁγίοις ἔταξαν ἑαυτούς·

records.literal_gloss: I urge and you, brothers; you know the household of Stephanas, that it is firstfruit of the Achaia and for service to the holy ones they appointed themselves;

en.L: Now I urge you, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} — you know the household of Stephanas, that it is [the] firstfruits of Achaia, and [that] they have devoted themselves to ministry for the holy ones —
en.B: I have a request, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}. You know the household of Stephanas: they were the first of the harvest in Achaia, and they have set themselves to serve God's holy people.
en.R: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, I want to ask you something. You know Stephanas and the people of his household. They were the first people in Achaia to become believers. And they have made it their work to help God's people.

fr.L: Or je vous exhorte, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} — vous connaissez la maison de Stéphanas, qu’elle est [les] prémices de l’Achaïe, et qu’ils se sont consacrés au ministère envers les saints —
fr.B: J’ai une demande à vous faire, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}. Vous connaissez la famille de Stéphanas : ils ont été le premier fruit de la moisson en Achaïe, et ils se sont mis au service du peuple saint de Dieu.
fr.R: {{gender:Frères et sœurs|Frères}}, j’ai quelque chose à vous demander. Vous connaissez Stéphanas et les gens de sa maison. Ils ont été les premiers en Achaïe à devenir croyants. Et ils se sont donné pour tâche d’aider le peuple de Dieu.

es.L: Ahora bien, {{plural_you:les|os}} ruego, hermanos (ya {{plural_you:conocen|conocéis}} la casa de Estéfanas, que es [las] primicias de Acaya, y [que] se han dedicado al servicio de los santos):
es.B: Tengo algo que {{plural_you:pedirles|pediros}}, hermanos. Ya {{plural_you:conocen|conocéis}} a la familia de Estéfanas: fueron las primicias de la cosecha en Acaya, y se han dedicado a servir al pueblo santo de Dios.
es.R: Hermanos, quiero {{plural_you:pedirles|pediros}} algo. {{plural_you:Ustedes conocen|Vosotros conocéis}} a Estéfanas y a los de su casa. Fueron los primeros en Acaya que llegaron a creer. Y se han dedicado a ayudar al pueblo de Dios.

decisions.choice: I urge you: the request itself comes in verse 16
decisions.reason: Paul begins "I urge you", breaks off to remind them about Stephanas's household, and gives the request in verse 16, which begins with ἵνα ("that").

decisions.choice: fellow believers, women and men
decisions.reason: ἀδελφοί addresses the whole church.

decisions.choice: the household of Stephanas
decisions.reason: A household included the family, slaves and others under its head. Paul baptized it himself (1:16), and Stephanas is with him now (verse 17).

decisions.choice: firstfruits: the first converts in Achaia, the first of a larger harvest
decisions.reason: ἀπαρχὴ is the first part of a harvest, given to God (Leviticus 23:10). Paul uses it of the first converts in a region (Romans 16:5). Achaia was the Roman province of southern Greece, with Corinth as its capital. Acts 17:34 tells of believers in Athens, also in Achaia, so Paul may mean the first household to believe, or the first of those who became the church's settled core.

decisions.choice: they devoted themselves: they took on this service of their own accord
decisions.reason: ἔταξαν ἑαυτούς means "they appointed themselves": no one assigned the task to them.

decisions.choice: service: practical help and care for the believers
decisions.reason: διακονίαν is service of any kind. Here it is most likely the care, hospitality and leadership Stephanas's household gave the church, as 12:5 speaks of different kinds of service.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The church included women and men. At the start of a Readable sentence the span is capitalized.

decisions.choice: ministry (L); serve (B); help (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the book-wide "ministry". Here the sense is practical service (m6), which "ministry" alone would make sound like preaching, so Balanced says "serve" and Readable "help".

decisions.choice: the first of the harvest (B); the first people ... to become believers (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the harvest picture in plain words, as in Romans 16:5; Readable says what it means (m4).

decisions.choice: holy ones (L); God's holy people (B); God's people (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide rendering of this word, as in 1:2: in current English "saints" suggests unusually good people, not a whole congregation.

decisions.choice: {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}; capitalised at the start of a Readable sentence
decisions.reason: As in English, the church is addressed as women and men together; "frères" stays available as the traditional form.

decisions.choice: [les] prémices (L), le premier fruit de la moisson (B); ministère (L), se mettre au service (B), aider (R); la maison (L, R), la famille (B)
decisions.reason: As in English and Romans 16:5: "prémices" is the French word for the first of a harvest, which Balanced puts in plain words. Literal keeps the book-wide "ministère"; Balanced and Readable say that practical service is meant (m6). "Maison" in the sense of household is understood, but Balanced says "famille", which a modern reader takes the same way.

decisions.choice: primicias (L, B); los primeros que llegaron a creer (R)
decisions.reason: As in 15:20; here the first converts of a larger harvest (m4).

decisions.choice: servicio (L); servir (B); ayudar (R)
decisions.reason: The word here means practical help and care for the believers (m6), so Spanish says "servicio", "servir", not "ministerio", which would suggest preaching.

source.text: ἵνα καὶ ὑμεῖς ὑποτάσσησθε τοῖς τοιούτοις καὶ παντὶ τῷ συνεργοῦντι καὶ κοπιῶντι.

records.literal_gloss: That also you be subject to the such [people] and to everyone the [one] working with [them] and laboring.

en.L: that you also submit to such [people], and to everyone who works with [them] and labors.
en.B: I urge you in turn to place yourselves under people like these, and under everyone who joins in the work and labors hard.
en.R: So I ask you to follow the lead of people like them, and of everyone who works hard with them.

fr.L: afin que vous aussi, vous vous soumettiez à de telles [personnes], et à quiconque travaille avec [eux] et peine.
fr.B: Je vous demande à votre tour de vous placer sous l’autorité de personnes comme celles-là, et de quiconque prend part au travail et s’y donne de la peine.
fr.R: Alors je vous demande de vous laisser guider par des gens comme eux, et par tous ceux qui travaillent dur avec eux.

es.L: que también {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:se sujeten|os sujetéis}} a tales [personas], y a todo el que colabora y trabaja.
es.B: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} pido que también {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:se pongan|os pongáis}} bajo la dirección de personas como estas, y de todo el que se une a la obra y trabaja duro.
es.R: Por eso {{plural_you:les|os}} pido que {{plural_you:sigan|sigáis}} el ejemplo y la dirección de personas como ellos, y de todos los que trabajan duro con ellos.

decisions.choice: the content of the request begun in verse 15; "you also" answers their service
decisions.reason: Stephanas's household gave themselves to serve the church; the church is to respond by accepting their lead.

decisions.choice: submit: accept the leadership of people who serve
decisions.reason: ὑποτάσσησθε is to put oneself under someone. Paul asks the church to recognize the leadership of those who serve, not to obey an appointed office; compare 1 Thessalonians 5:12-13.

decisions.choice: works with them: shares in the work with Stephanas's household
decisions.reason: συνεργοῦντι means to work together, without saying with whom. In context it most likely means those who work alongside the household just named. κοπιῶντι is hard labor, Paul's word for work in the gospel (15:10).

decisions.choice: I urge you (B); I ask you (R)
decisions.reason: Verse 15 is a separate record, so Balanced and Readable repeat the request it began (m1).

decisions.choice: sujetarse
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "sujetarse", the verb used for the same Greek word in 14:32, 34; Balanced and Readable say what it means here, accepting the leadership of people who serve (m2).

source.text: χαίρω δὲ ἐπὶ τῇ παρουσίᾳ Στεφανᾶ καὶ Φορτουνάτου καὶ Ἀχαϊκοῦ, ὅτι τὸ ὑμέτερον ὑστέρημα οὗτοι ἀνεπλήρωσαν, ἀνέπαυσαν γὰρ τὸ ἐμὸν πνεῦμα καὶ τὸ ὑμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: I rejoice and at the arrival of Stephanas and Fortunatus and Achaicus, because the your lack these filled up, \v 18 they refreshed for the my spirit and the of you.

en.L: And I rejoice over the arrival of Stephanas and Fortunatus and Achaicus, because these have filled up your lack; \v 18 for they refreshed my spirit and yours.
en.B: It makes me glad that Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus are here, because they have filled the gap your absence left. \v 18 They have refreshed me in spirit, and you as well.
en.R: I am happy that Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus came here. I could not be with all of you, but having them here was almost like having you. \v 18 They have cheered me up, just as they cheered you up.

fr.L: Et je me réjouis de la venue de Stéphanas, de Fortunat et d’Achaïque, parce que ceux-ci ont comblé votre manque ; \v 18 car ils ont réconforté mon esprit et le vôtre.
fr.B: Je suis heureux que Stéphanas, Fortunat et Achaïque soient ici, car ils ont comblé le vide que votre absence laissait. \v 18 Ils ont réconforté mon esprit, et le vôtre aussi.
fr.R: Je suis content que Stéphanas, Fortunat et Achaïque soient venus ici. Je ne pouvais pas être avec vous tous, mais en les ayant ici, c’était presque comme si vous étiez là. \v 18 Ils m’ont redonné du courage, comme ils vous en ont redonné à vous aussi.

es.L: Y me alegro por la venida de Estéfanas, de Fortunato y de Acaico, porque estos han suplido {{plural_you:la falta de ustedes|vuestra falta}}; \v 18 pues han confortado mi espíritu y el {{plural_you:de ustedes|vuestro}}.
es.B: Me alegra que Estéfanas, Fortunato y Acaico estén aquí, porque han llenado el vacío que dejaba {{plural_you:la ausencia de ustedes|vuestra ausencia}}. \v 18 Me han reanimado el espíritu, y a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} también.
es.R: Estoy contento de que Estéfanas, Fortunato y Acaico hayan venido. Yo no podía estar con todos {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, pero tenerlos aquí ha sido casi como {{plural_you:tenerlos|teneros}} a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. \v 18 Me han animado mucho, igual que {{plural_you:los|os}} animaron a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

decisions.choice: three men from Corinth who came to Paul in Ephesus
decisions.reason: They probably brought the Corinthians' letter (7:1) and would take this one back. Fortunatus is a Latin name and Achaicus means "man of Achaia"; such names were often given to slaves or freed slaves, so they may have belonged to Stephanas's household, but the text does not say.

decisions.choice: arrival, presence
decisions.reason: παρουσίᾳ is the ordinary word for someone's arrival or presence. Paul uses it of Christ's coming in 15:23, but here of these men.

decisions.choice: your lack: Paul's not having the church with him
alternatives: what you failed to do for me
decisions.reason: ὑστέρημα is what is missing. Paul most likely means that their visit made up for his separation from the church, not that the church had failed him.

decisions.choice: refreshed: gave new strength and rest
decisions.reason: ἀνέπαυσαν is to give rest or relief (2 Corinthians 7:13; Philemon 7, 20). "And yours" probably means that the church too was refreshed by their faithful service, or will be when they bring Paul's reply.

decisions.choice: filled the gap your absence left (B); I could not be with all of you, but having them here was almost like having you (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what was lacking (m3).

decisions.choice: Fortunat, Achaïque
decisions.reason: The usual French forms of the two names, as French writes Épaïnète and Aquilas.

source.text: ἐπιγινώσκετε οὖν τοὺς τοιούτους.

records.literal_gloss: Recognize therefore the such [people].

en.L: Therefore recognize such [people].
en.B: Make sure, then, that people like these are honored.
en.R: So show respect to people like them.

fr.L: Reconnaissez donc de telles [personnes].
fr.B: Sachez donc honorer des gens comme eux.
fr.R: Alors, montrez du respect à des gens comme eux.

es.L: {{plural_you:Reconozcan|Reconoced}}, pues, a tales [personas].
es.B: {{plural_you:Procuren|Procurad}}, pues, que personas como estas sean honradas.
es.R: Así que {{plural_you:muestren|mostrad}} respeto a personas como ellos.

decisions.choice: recognize: acknowledge their worth and honor them
decisions.reason: ἐπιγινώσκετε here means to give due recognition, as 1 Thessalonians 5:12 asks for those who labor among the believers.

source.text: Ἀσπάζονται ὑμᾶς αἱ ἐκκλησίαι τῆς Ἀσίας.

records.literal_gloss: Greet you the churches of the Asia.

en.L: The churches of Asia greet you.
en.B: Greetings to you from the churches of Asia.
en.R: The churches in the province of Asia say hello.

fr.L: Les églises de l’Asie vous saluent.
fr.B: Les églises d’Asie vous adressent leurs salutations.
fr.R: Les églises de la province d’Asie vous disent bonjour.

es.L: {{plural_you:Los|Os}} saludan las iglesias de Asia.
es.B: Saludos de parte de las iglesias de Asia.
es.R: Las iglesias de la provincia de Asia {{plural_you:les|os}} mandan saludos.

decisions.choice: Asia: the Roman province in the west of what is now Turkey
decisions.reason: Ephesus was its chief city. From there the gospel spread through the province (Acts 19:10), to churches such as Colossae and Laodicea (Colossians 4:13-16).

decisions.choice: the province of Asia
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that a Roman province is meant (m1).

decisions.choice: say hello
decisions.reason: Readable uses everyday words for a greeting, as in Colossians 4:10.

source.text: ἀσπάζεται ὑμᾶς ἐν κυρίῳ πολλὰ Ἀκύλας καὶ Πρίσκα σὺν τῇ κατ’ οἶκον αὐτῶν ἐκκλησίᾳ.

records.literal_gloss: Greet you in [the] Lord much Aquila and Prisca with the at house of them church.

en.L: Aquila and Prisca greet you warmly in [the] Lord, with the church at their house.
en.B: Warm greetings in the Lord from Aquila and Prisca and from the church that meets in their house.
en.R: Aquila and Prisca, who belong to the Lord as you do, send you warm greetings. So does the church that meets in their home.

fr.L: Aquilas et Prisca vous saluent chaleureusement dans le Seigneur, avec l’église qui [est] dans leur maison.
fr.B: Aquilas et Prisca vous adressent de chaleureuses salutations dans le Seigneur, ainsi que l’église qui se réunit chez eux.
fr.R: Aquilas et Prisca, qui appartiennent au Seigneur comme vous, vous envoient leurs salutations chaleureuses. L’église qui se réunit dans leur maison vous salue aussi.

es.L: {{plural_you:Los|Os}} saludan mucho en [el] Señor Aquila y Prisca, con la iglesia que [se reúne] en su casa.
es.B: Muchos saludos en el Señor de parte de Aquila y Prisca, y de la iglesia que se reúne en su casa.
es.R: Aquila y Prisca, que pertenecen al Señor como {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, {{plural_you:les|os}} mandan muchos saludos. También la iglesia que se reúne en su casa.

decisions.choice: Aquila and Prisca: a Jewish couple who had worked with Paul in Corinth
decisions.reason: They met Paul in Corinth after Claudius expelled the Jews from Rome, worked with him at tentmaking, and then went with him to Ephesus (Acts 18:1-3, 18-26). The Corinthians knew them well. Acts calls her Priscilla, the familiar form of the name; Paul calls her Prisca (Romans 16:3).

decisions.choice: the church in their house: believers who met in their home
decisions.reason: The first churches met in homes (Romans 16:5; Colossians 4:15). In Ephesus, as later in Rome, a group met in the couple's house.

decisions.choice: warmly, in the Lord: the greeting of fellow believers
decisions.reason: πολλὰ ("much") makes the greeting warm, and "in the Lord" marks it as the greeting of people who belong to the Lord together.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: the greeting ends with the church in their house
alternatives: some manuscripts add "with whom I am staying"
decisions.reason: Some Greek-Latin manuscripts add that Paul was lodging with Aquila and Prisca, which fits Acts 18:3 but is not in the older manuscripts. Some manuscripts also spell her name Priscilla, as in Acts. (From general knowledge of the manuscripts; reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.)

decisions.choice: Prisca
decisions.reason: The levels keep Paul's form of the name, as in Romans 16:3 (m1).

decisions.choice: the church that meets in their house (B); home (R)
decisions.reason: The church is the people, not the building; "meets" says so, as in Romans 16:5.

decisions.choice: who belong to the Lord as you do
decisions.reason: Readable says what "in the Lord" adds to the greeting (m3).

source.text: ἀσπάζονται ὑμᾶς οἱ ἀδελφοὶ πάντες.

records.literal_gloss: Greet you the brothers all.

en.L: All the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} greet you.
en.B: All the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} here send you greetings.
en.R: All the believers here send you their greetings.

fr.L: Tous les {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} vous saluent.
fr.B: Tous les {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} d’ici vous adressent leurs salutations.
fr.R: Tous les croyants d’ici vous envoient leurs salutations.

es.L: {{plural_you:Los|Os}} saludan todos los hermanos.
es.B: Todos los hermanos de aquí {{plural_you:les|os}} mandan saludos.
es.R: Todos los creyentes de aquí {{plural_you:les|os}} mandan saludos.

decisions.choice: all the believers where Paul is, women and men
decisions.reason: After the churches of Asia and the church in Aquila and Prisca's house, "all the brothers" is most likely the believers in Ephesus as a whole.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The believers included women and men. Readable says "believers", which needs no setting.

decisions.choice: here
decisions.reason: Those who send greetings are the believers where Paul is writing (m1).

source.text: ἀσπάσασθε ἀλλήλους ἐν φιλήματι ἁγίῳ.

records.literal_gloss: Greet one another with kiss holy.

en.L: Greet one another with a holy kiss.
en.B: Greet one another with a holy kiss.
en.R: When you greet each other, give each other a holy kiss.

fr.L: Saluez-vous les uns les autres par un saint baiser.
fr.B: Saluez-vous les uns les autres d’un saint baiser.
fr.R: Quand vous vous saluez, donnez-vous les uns aux autres un saint baiser.

es.L: {{plural_you:Salúdense|Saludaos}} unos a otros con un beso santo.
es.B: {{plural_you:Salúdense|Saludaos}} unos a otros con un beso santo.
es.R: Cuando {{plural_you:se saluden|os saludéis}}, {{plural_you:dense|daos}} unos a otros un beso santo.

decisions.choice: a holy kiss: the greeting of family members, shared by believers as God's family
decisions.reason: A kiss on the cheek was a common greeting between relatives and close friends in the ancient Mediterranean world. Believers greeted one another this way as members of one family (Romans 16:16; 2 Corinthians 13:12; 1 Thessalonians 5:26; 1 Peter 5:14). "Holy" marks it as belonging to God's people, pure and without romantic meaning. In a church divided into parties (1:10-12), the command is pointed.

decisions.choice: kiss
decisions.reason: We keep the custom Paul names rather than replacing it with a modern one, as in 2 Corinthians 13:12; meaning decision m1 explains it.

source.text: Ὁ ἀσπασμὸς τῇ ἐμῇ χειρὶ Παύλου.

records.literal_gloss: The greeting with the my [own] hand of Paul.

en.L: The greeting [is] in my own hand, Paul's.
en.B: I, Paul, am adding this greeting with my own hand.
en.R: Now I, Paul, am writing this greeting myself, with my own hand.

fr.L: La salutation [est] de ma propre main, [celle] de Paul.
fr.B: Moi, Paul, j’ajoute cette salutation de ma propre main.
fr.R: Maintenant, moi, Paul, j’écris moi-même cette salutation, de ma propre main.

es.L: El saludo [es] de mi propia mano, de Pablo.
es.B: Yo, Pablo, escribo este saludo de mi propia mano.
es.R: Ahora yo, Pablo, escribo este saludo yo mismo, con mi propia mano.

decisions.choice: Paul signs the letter in his own hand; someone else wrote the rest
decisions.reason: Paul usually dictated his letters to someone who wrote them down (Romans 16:22), and then added a greeting in his own handwriting as a mark that the letter was really his (Galatians 6:11; Colossians 4:18; 2 Thessalonians 3:17). The verses that follow are in his own hand.

decisions.choice: I, Paul, am adding this greeting (B); Now I, Paul, am writing (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek has no verb; Balanced and Readable turn the note into a sentence, as in Colossians 4:18.

source.text: εἴ τις οὐ φιλεῖ τὸν κύριον, ἤτω ἀνάθεμα.

records.literal_gloss: If anyone not loves the Lord, let him be accursed.

en.L: If anyone does not love the Lord, let {{gender:them|him}} be accursed.
en.B: A curse on anyone who does not love the Lord!
en.R: May God's curse be on anyone who does not love the Lord.

fr.L: Si quelqu’un n’aime pas le Seigneur, qu’il soit maudit.
fr.B: Maudit soit quiconque n’aime pas le Seigneur !
fr.R: Que la malédiction de Dieu soit sur quiconque n’aime pas le Seigneur.

es.L: Si alguno no ama al Señor, sea anatema.
es.B: ¡Maldito sea el que no ama al Señor!
es.R: Que caiga la maldición de Dios sobre el que no ama al Señor.

decisions.choice: accursed: under God's curse, handed over to destruction
decisions.reason: ἀνάθεμα is the word of 12:3: what the Greek Old Testament calls devoted to destruction (Deuteronomy 7:26). Paul uses it for one cut off and under God's curse (Romans 9:3; Galatians 1:8-9).

decisions.choice: love: heartfelt love and loyalty
decisions.reason: Paul usually uses another verb for love; φιλεῖ is the word for warm affection between friends. Its use here may come from a set form of words used in worship. To not love the Lord is to have no part with him.

decisions.choice: a solemn curse formula, leaving judgment to God
decisions.reason: ἤτω is a third-person command, "let him be". It solemnly declares that whoever does not love the Lord stands under God's judgment; it does not call on the readers to act. The prayer that follows asks for the Lord who will judge to come (4:5).

decisions.choice: the Lord: Jesus
decisions.reason: The next sentence prays for "our Lord" to come, and verse 23 names him: the Lord Jesus.

decisions.choice: {{gender:them|him}}
decisions.reason: "Anyone" includes women and men; Balanced and Readable need no pronoun.

decisions.choice: A curse on (B); May God's curse be on (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "accursed" and Balanced and Readable "curse", the words of 12:3 ("Jesus is cursed"). Readable says whose curse it is (m1).

decisions.choice: "quelqu’un … qu’il soit maudit" (L), with no gender setting; maudit (L, B), la malédiction de Dieu (R)
decisions.reason: The English needs {{gender:them|him}} at Literal; in French "quelqu’un" already means anyone, and the "il" that refers back to it is ordinary generic French, so no span is used. "Anathème" copies the Greek word but is church jargon; "maudit" says the sense (m1) and matches the curse of 12:3.

decisions.choice: sea anatema (L); maldito sea (B); la maldición de Dios (R)
decisions.reason: The word means placed under God's curse (m1). Literal keeps "anatema", the Greek word that Spanish has borrowed; Balanced and Readable say "maldito", "maldición". "El que" and "alguno" cover anyone, so the English gender span has nothing to change.

source.text: Μαράνα θά.

records.literal_gloss: Marana tha (Our Lord, come).

en.L: Marana tha!
en.B: Our Lord, come!
en.R: Our Lord Jesus, come!

fr.L: Marana tha !
fr.B: Notre Seigneur, viens !
fr.R: Notre Seigneur Jésus, viens !

es.L: ¡Marana tha!
es.B: ¡Señor nuestro, ven!
es.R: ¡Ven, Señor nuestro Jesús!

decisions.choice: an Aramaic prayer, kept in its original language
decisions.reason: Μαράνα θά is Aramaic, the language of the first believers in Judea, written in Greek letters. Paul does not translate it, so the Corinthians already knew it, probably from worship. The Didache, an early Christian writing, has the same words in a prayer at the Lord's Supper (Didache 10:6).

decisions.choice: a prayer: "Our Lord, come!"
decisions.reason: Ancient manuscripts were written without spaces between words, so the division is an editor's decision. The SBLGNT divides the letters as Μαράνα θά, which means "Our Lord, come!". Divided another way they mean "Our Lord has come" or "is coming". The prayer "Come, Lord Jesus" in Revelation 22:20 and the Lord's Supper kept "until he comes" (11:26) favor the prayer, but the statement is possible.

decisions.choice: the earliest believers prayed to Jesus as Lord
decisions.reason: The words come from the Aramaic-speaking church, before the gospel reached the Greek world. Already there believers called Jesus "our Lord" and prayed to him to come.

decisions.choice: Marana tha (L); Our Lord, come (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Aramaic words, as Galatians 4:6 keeps "Abba", written in English letters with the SBLGNT's division into two words. Balanced and Readable give the meaning (m2).

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: The Lord prayed to is Jesus, named in verse 23 and in Revelation 22:20.

source.text: ἡ χάρις τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ μεθ’ ὑμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: The grace of the Lord Jesus [be] with you.

en.L: The grace of the Lord Jesus [be] with you.
en.B: May the grace of the Lord Jesus be with you.
en.R: I pray that the Lord Jesus will be with you in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} grace.

fr.L: La grâce du Seigneur Jésus [soit] avec vous.
fr.B: Que la grâce du Seigneur Jésus soit avec vous.
fr.R: Je prie pour que le Seigneur Jésus soit avec vous et vous accorde {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} grâce.

es.L: La gracia del Señor Jesús [sea] con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.B: Que la gracia del Señor Jesús esté con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.R: Pido que el Señor Jesús esté con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} con {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} gracia.

decisions.choice: a prayer: may grace be with you
alternatives: a statement: grace is with you
decisions.reason: There is no verb. As in the closing of Paul's other letters, it is a blessing prayed over the readers (2 Corinthians 13:13; Philippians 4:23).

decisions.choice: the letter ends where it began, with the grace of the Lord Jesus
decisions.reason: Paul opened with grace and peace (1:3) and thanked God for the grace given in Christ (1:4). After a curse on those who do not love the Lord, the last word is his grace.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "the Lord Jesus"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "Christ", as copyists often filled out the name. (From general knowledge of the manuscripts; reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.)

decisions.choice: I pray that the Lord Jesus will be with you in his grace
alternatives: the grace of the Lord Jesus be with you
decisions.reason: Readable states the blessing as the prayer it is (m1) and keeps the key term.

source.text: ἡ ἀγάπη μου μετὰ πάντων ὑμῶν ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: The love of me with all of you in Christ Jesus.

en.L: My love [be] with all of you in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus.
en.B: I send my love to every one of you in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus.
en.R: I love every one of you, because we all belong to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus.

fr.L: Mon amour [soit] avec vous tous {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} Jésus.
fr.B: Je vous assure tous de mon amour {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} Jésus.
fr.R: Je vous aime, chacun de vous, parce que nous appartenons tous au {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus.

es.L: Mi amor [sea] con todos {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} en {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}} Jesús.
es.B: Mi amor está con todos {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} en {{christos:Cristo Jesús|el Mesías Jesús}}.
es.R: {{plural_you:Los|Os}} amo a todos {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, porque todos pertenecemos {{christos:a Cristo Jesús|al Mesías Jesús}}.

decisions.choice: Paul's love for all of them, without exception
decisions.reason: There is no verb: it may be a wish ("be with") or a statement ("is with"). Paul ends no other letter with his own love. After a letter that rebuked the church sharply, he assures every one of them, whatever party they took (1:12), of his love.

decisions.choice: in Christ Jesus: Paul's love belongs to their shared life in Christ
alternatives: only describing "you": you who are in Christ
decisions.reason: The phrase goes with the whole sentence: Paul loves them as one who, like them, belongs to Christ Jesus.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: no "Amen" at the end
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "Amen", as copyists often did at the end of a book, and the King James Version has it. Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: I send my love to
decisions.reason: The Greek has no verb; Balanced makes it a natural closing.

decisions.choice: because we all belong to Christ Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable says what "in Christ Jesus" adds (m2).

decisions.choice: {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} Jésus (L, B); au {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus (R)
decisions.reason: As in Colossians: French cannot say "en Messie", so the span for "in Christ" covers the preposition; elsewhere the article stays outside the span.
